THE BRIEF

We look after the outdoor areas that form part of a commercial property’s daily operation. We review planting, irrigation, presentation and pedestrian access together, then separate routine grounds care from repairs or a larger landscape change. The agreed tasks and waste arrangements are clear before attendance.

✺

THE WORK

Begin with how the outdoor area is used

  • Entrances and shared routes

    We review garden edges, planted areas and irrigation beside the routes used by guests, staff and deliveries. The maintenance plan keeps the work area and everyday movement in view.

  • Courtyards and resort grounds

    We identify the presentation tasks, planting condition and any repair items. Furniture, facility opening times and equipment access influence how a visit is staged.

  • Irrigation symptoms

    We record leaking points, uneven coverage and spray reaching paths or neighbouring surfaces. Existing zones and accessible components help define the investigation and repair list.

THE WORK

Choose materials for the actual site

  • Irrigation components

    We identify the existing arrangement and accessible components before selecting replacements. A changed spray pattern or repeated leak may require checking neighbouring parts and the zone operation.

  • Planting and finishes

    Planting changes, mulch and other agreed materials are considered against the existing landscape, exposure and use. Larger paving, drainage or structural work is identified as a separate scope.

THE WORK

An ordered visit from inspection to clean-up

  1. 01

    Walk the agreed areas

    We confirm the priority areas, routine tasks and repair items with your manager before equipment and materials are positioned.

  2. 02

    Complete the agreed tasks

    We carry out the specified grounds and irrigation work, separating completed maintenance from further repair or design requirements.

  3. 03

    Check and clear the area

    We review the completed areas and relevant irrigation operation, then remove the agreed green waste and return access as planned.

THE WORK

Guests and pedestrians stay part of the plan

We agree work zones, watering arrangements, equipment movement and temporary route changes around occupied facilities. For a larger courtyard update, the brief identifies which areas remain available and how material deliveries and waste leave the property.

THE WORK

A maintenance list you can review

  • Quotation factors

    Area, access, planting condition, irrigation faults, materials, visit frequency and green waste quantities affect the scope. Repairs are itemised alongside any regular care arrangement.

  • Completion and follow-up

    We record the areas attended, tasks completed and agreed irrigation checks. Any ongoing plant issue, unavailable component or larger change is identified for the next decision.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Does regular garden care include irrigation repairs?+

The plan states the routine tasks and agreed irrigation checks. Parts, repairs or wider system changes are itemised so they are not assumed to be included in every maintenance visit.

Can grounds work take place while a resort is open?+

We review the facility layout, guest routes and equipment requirements. Where practical, the work is staged around agreed areas and opening times, with access arrangements confirmed in advance.

Can you look at paving or drainage beside the garden?+

We can include the reported issue in the site brief. Grounds care, irrigation work and the relevant paving or drainage scope are then clearly separated and coordinated.

Why does paving stay wet after irrigation?+

Overspray, poor drainage or a leak can each contribute. Record the affected zone and when the surface becomes wet.
